root_cause.text: On UP kernels (!CONFIG_SMP), spin_trylock() is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds, so kmalloc_nolock() called from NMI context can re-enter the slab allocator and acquire the n->list_lock already held by the interrupted context, corrupting slab state.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "On UP kernels (!CONFIG_SMP), spin_trylock() is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds even when the lock is already held. As a result, kmalloc_nolock() called from NMI context can re-enter the slab allocator and acquire n->list_lock that the interrupted context is already holding, corrupting slab state." The patch adds a check `if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_SMP) && in_nmi()) return NULL;` to prevent this re-entry.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition restricts the NMI/hardirq re-entry guard to PREEMPT_RT kernels only, leaving non-PREEMPT_RT (especially UP) kernels unprotected. On UP, spin_trylock() is a no-op that always succeeds, so an NMI can re-enter the slab allocator without this check, leading to corruption.
This return NULL only executes when the PREEMPT_RT condition holds. On non-PREEMPT_RT kernels, the code falls through to the retry path, allowing NMI re-entrance into the slab allocator.

The retry label marks the start of the unprotected allocation path that is reached when the NMI check fails (or is not present). On UP kernels, entering this label from NMI context enables re-acquisition of locks already held by the interrupted context, corrupting slab state.

This size check does not prevent NMI re-entrance; it is part of the unprotected flow that can be reached from NMI on UP kernels. If the size is within limits, execution continues deeper into the allocator where lock re-acquisition occurs.

This return NULL (associated with the size overflow check) does not mitigate the NMI re-entrance vulnerability on non-PREEMPT_RT systems. It only handles the case of oversized allocations, but when the size is valid the allocation proceeds unprotected.
